answer: The system earns weight for an identity only when its work history stays distinct over 30 days, and near-identical timing or error patterns are clustered and lose weight together. Each identity carries its sealed box across a 25-meter bridge in one timed trip and opens it on a jetty where the crossing time is recorded to the second. A ferrous tag for that identity is weighed in the box at 10 grams, and an identity matching another on tag weight, crossing time within 5 seconds, and error pattern counts as the same operator, so 100 fakes need 100 separate crossings.
